title: Regression: slugify keeps separator runs and edge hyphens
statement: Regression report for slugkit.slugify(text). Since the last change the function returns 'hello--world' for 'Hello--World', 'a---b' for 'a -- b' and 'end-' for 'end!'. The intended behaviour, which the existing tests only partly cover, is: lower-case the text; every maximal run of one or more characters that are not ASCII letters a-z or ASCII digits 0-9 becomes exactly one hyphen; leading and trailing hyphens are removed; an input with no ASCII letters or digits (including the empty string and whitespace-only text) returns ''. Non-ASCII letters such as 'é' are separators, not kept characters (so 'café crème' is 'caf-cr-me'). Keep raising TypeError for non-string input, keep returning a str, and keep the existing tests in tests/ passing without modifying them. Fix the regression in slugkit/core.py.
acceptance_criteria: slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world', slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b', slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three', slugify('x___y') == 'x-y' (runs of separators collapse to one hyphen).
slugify('end!') == 'end', slugify('  padded  ') == 'padded', slugify('--both--') == 'both', slugify('(parens)') == 'parens' (no leading or trailing hyphen).
slugify('') == '', slugify('!!!') == '', slugify('   ') == '' (nothing to keep gives the empty string).

Existing behaviour is preserved: slugify('Hello World') == 'hello-world', slugify('already-a-slug') == 'already-a-slug', slugify('Python 3') == 'python-3', slugify('MiXeD CaSe 42') == 'mixed-case-42'.
Non-ASCII letters are separators: slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me' and slugify('日本語') == ''.
The result is a str; TypeError for non-string input such as None, 3, 2.5, ['a'] and b'bytes'.
